html:
SMTO-ART-0011 — SMTO won't save a file from this location

GUID: 1eb4068c-ff3d-4e64-a9bc-25f43fc6a280
Slug: artifact-unsafe-path
Domain: ART · Subsystem: art

What happened

  • This file's location isn't safe for SMTO to collect. It's outside the Task's own folders, goes through a shortcut link, or isn't a normal file, so SMTO didn't copy it.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Ask SMTO in the conversation to save the finished file as a regular file in the Task's output folder, not through a link or shortcut. SMTO only collects real files inside the Task's own folders, so a link can't point it at other files on the computer.
  2. If you give the file name yourself, use a simple name inside that folder, such as reports/summary.csv, without '..' or a drive letter like C:. Names that climb out of the folder or point to another drive are refused to keep the computer's other files private.
  3. Then open Artifacts from this run and select Retry collection if it appears, or ask SMTO to save the file again. SMTO checks the new location the same way and collects the file once it is a normal file in the right place.

What success looks like

  • The file appears in Artifacts from this run without an error.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages SMTO, with the file's location. Don't create links or change folder permissions to get around this check.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • Artifact path validation rejected the source: traversal, absolute, drive or control-character syntax, a symlink or reparse point on the path, a non-regular file, an excluded internal name, or a temp reference outside the run's eligible temp roots.

What this means

  • Path validation rejects traversal/drive/control syntax, symlink/reparse boundaries, nonregular files or a temporary reference outside eligible roots. Artifact publication and presentation remain separate from the command that produced a file. Only an explicit pre-dispatch rejection proves that new command did not run; diagnostics do not collect, transfer, quarantine or delete files.

Why this can happen

  • Path validation rejects traversal/drive/control syntax, symlink/reparse boundaries, nonregular files or a temporary reference outside eligible roots.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect the exact path component/type and owning workspace without disabling containment checks.

How to fix it

  • Check the diagnostic in the collection status or Gateway log (outside workspace, symlinked directory or source, non-regular file, or temp reference outside OF_RUN_TEMP_DIR and the OS temp roots). Have the task write a regular file under OF_RUN_ARTIFACT_DIR or OF_RUN_TEMP_DIR and collect again; keep relative_path and contained_path checks intact.
  • Use a regular supported path inside the owning artifact workspace; retain boundary and symlink protections.

Retry and execution caution

  • Correct the recorded cause, then inspect current state and existing receipts before requesting another attempt.

How to verify the fix

  • A regular supported contained source passes the same boundary protections.

What not to do

  • Do not silently substitute a different target for a saved run or move its existing execution authority.

Technical notes

  • Artifact publication and presentation remain separate from the command that produced a file. Only an explicit pre-dispatch rejection proves that new command did not run; diagnostics do not collect, transfer, quarantine or delete files.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
